source.title: SemEval-2025 Task 4: Unlearning sensitive content from Large Language Models
source.authors: Anil Ramakrishna; Yixin Wan; Xiaomeng Jin; Kai-Wei Chang; Zhi-Qi Bu; Bhanukiran Vinzamuri; V. Cevher; Ming-Yi Hong; Rahul Gupta

record.tranche_reason: It evaluates whether unlearning reduces performance on targeted content while retaining utility, using a new benchmark and measures. It does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for benchmarked unlearning methods and participant systems on forget/retain memorization metrics and MMLU utility. It does not apply fine-tuning recovery attacks, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. Detailed per-task participant scores are not separately extracted where the flattened table layout does not reliably assign values.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks unlearning methods and more than 24 participant systems on OLMo 7B and 1B models fine-tuned to memorize synthetic and real documents. It reports forget-set regurgitation and knowledge scores alongside retain-set scores and MMLU utility. This bears on the first half of version A (forgetting while keeping general ability) in a new setting. It applies no recovery attacks, so the attack-resistance part of A and versions B–F are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say most systems struggle to keep utility while completely unlearning. Even the top team lost MMLU (0.494 to 0.443) and produced garbage tokens on some prompts. Teams that kept utility did not improve MIA or task-aggregate scores. They call balancing utility and unlearning an open problem.
record.recipe_differences: The paper benchmarks several unlearning algorithms and participant systems on synthetic creative works, synthetic PII biographies, and real biographies. It measures forget/retain performance and utility, rather than testing post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported aggregate pattern differs by model size: selected settings over-unlearned on 7B and under-unlearned on 1B. The paper also notes a utility trade-off for the top 7B system.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-based membership-inference scores after unlearning are near zero for most teams. ZJUKLAB scores 0.048 and YNU 0.139 despite high forget scores. Authors read ZJUKLAB's result as information not fully removed from parameter space.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning that suppresses regurgitation and QA accuracy can leave membership-inference-detectable traces of the forget set.

record.problems: The paper reports over- and under-unlearning in aggregate for the benchmarked settings without assigning that summary to individual algorithms. It does not test recovery attacks. Some detailed task-level results appear in flattened tables or figures.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed participant task-by-task forget/retain scores in Table 4 and per-epoch benchmark values in Figures 1, 6, and 7 were not extracted as separate rows because the flattened values or figure traces do not provide reliably assignable exact values here. MIA scores were omitted because they are membership-inference measurements, not one of the recovery behaviors specified by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks fail to recover the forgotten information; no recovery attack is applied (MIA measures membership leakage, not recovery).
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All: no activation ablation or mechanistic analysis of blocked versus deleted knowledge.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
All: no method is claimed to resist recovery attacks.

missing.what: Per-team forget and retain regurgitation and knowledge scores for the top-5 7B systems. The table is readable: knowledge values run column-wise. Example: YNU forget scores are about 0.90–1.00 with retain knowledge 0.967/0.984/0.970. Example: Mr. Snuffleupagus retain Task 2 knowledge is 0.167.
MMLU for the other top 7B teams (ZJUKLAB 0.471, YNU 0.436, Mr. Snuffleupagus 0.485, ishumei 0.481) against base 0.494. Also SHA256 at MMLU 0.275 with task aggregate 0.964.
Task aggregate and MIA scores per team, showing the forgetting versus leakage trade-off.

record.verdict_notes: This is a SemEval task summary, not an original source. All evidence concerns forgetting versus utility on memorized fine-tuned documents, not hazardous knowledge. The forget metrics are 1 minus regurgitation/accuracy against the fine-tuned model, not a near-chance accuracy. Reclassified from T2 to T3 because the setting is new (memorized synthetic and real documents, PII). Rows are thin: the readable Table 3 and Table 4 values should be added.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks fail to recover the information; the paper does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting.
Recovery by fine-tuning on small, unrelated, loosely related, or subset data.
Recovery by ablating an activation direction or evidence that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Recovery by prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Whether a newer method resists the recovery attacks above.

rows.subject: OLMo-7B-0724-Instruct-hf
rows.operation_detail: Benchmarked Gradient Ascent, Gradient Difference, KL Regularization, and Negative Preference Optimization for 10 epochs with learning rate = 1e − 5 and batch size 32.

conditions.value: Gradient Ascent, Gradient Difference, KL Regularization, Negative Preference Optimization

rows.measure: Regurgitation and knowledge performance on forget and retain subsets
rows.value: The authors report over-unlearning with the 7B model for the selected hyperparameters.
rows.note: The text gives an overall description of the selected 7B settings; it does not assign this outcome to each algorithm separately or provide exact values in the text.
rows.check: Organizer baselines on 7B at the stated hyperparameters. Authors report over-unlearning: forgetting is achieved but retain performance is lost too. The value is a text summary only; the Figure 1 traces are not readable per algorithm.

rows.subject: OLMo-1B-0724-hf
rows.operation_detail: Benchmarked Gradient Ascent, Gradient Difference, KL Regularization, and Negative Preference Optimization for 10 epochs with learning rate = 1e − 5 and batch size 32.

conditions.value: Gradient Ascent, Gradient Difference, KL Regularization, Negative Preference Optimization

rows.measure: Regurgitation and knowledge performance on forget and retain subsets
rows.value: The authors report under-unlearning with the 1B model for the selected hyperparameters.
rows.note: The text gives an overall description of the selected 1B settings; it does not assign this outcome to each algorithm separately or provide exact values in the text.
rows.check: Under-unlearning on 1B means forget-set scores stay high. Figure 1's 1B y-axes span about 0.94–1.00, so little forgetting occurred. 'absent' fits better than 'partial', though exact values cannot be read.

rows.subject: AILS-NTUA unlearned 7B model
rows.operation_detail: Participant unlearning system; the paper describes it as gradient-based unlearning with LoRA adapters and forget/retain data mixing.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a notable utility drop despite the team's high unlearning scores.
rows.check: Correct values: MMLU 0.494 to 0.443. Forget scores (Table 4) are near-perfect, but retain regurgitation drops to 0.493 and 0.556 on Tasks 1 and 3. The authors also report garbage tokens on some prompts. Forgetting is achieved at a utility cost.

rows.subject: AILS-NTUA unlearned 1B model
rows.operation_detail: Participant unlearning system; the paper describes it as gradient-based unlearning with LoRA adapters and forget/retain data mixing.
rows.note: The paper says the 1B base model's MMLU performance was already close to random chance, but does not give its exact baseline here.
rows.check: The 1B base model's MMLU is near chance (exact baseline not given), so this measure cannot show a utility cost.

relationships.condition: Organizer baseline algorithms (GA, GD, KL, NPO) at the fixed hyperparameters, 7B and 1B
relationships.reason: The fixed settings over-unlearn on 7B (r1) and barely unlearn on 1B (r2), so success depends on the hyperparameter choice.
relationships.display_finding: Fixed hyperparameters caused excessive unlearning on 7B but barely produced forgetting on 1B.

relationships.condition: Top participant systems on the 7B model
relationships.reason: AILS-NTUA reaches near-perfect forget scores, but MMLU falls from 0.494 to 0.443 and retain regurgitation drops to about 0.5 (r3; Table 4 per text). SHA256 forgets well but MMLU falls to 0.275.
relationships.display_finding: AILS-NTUA achieved near-perfect forgetting while MMLU fell from 0.494 to 0.443 and retain regurgitation reached about 0.5; SHA256 reduced MMLU to 0.275.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Selected benchmark hyperparameters on the 7B and 1B models
reader_labels.reason: The benchmark reports over-unlearning on 7B and under-unlearning on 1B, so the selected settings do not show a consistent balance of targeted forgetting and retained performance (r1, r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The top-performing team's MMLU accuracy fell from 0.494 to 0.443 despite its high unlearning scores (r3).
